Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 69 of 2008
Revisionist :- Kamlesh

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Revisionist :- Rajendra Prasad Verma,Avinash Srivastava
Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt. Advocate
Hon'ble Dinesh Kumar Singh,J.
1.

This Criminal Revision under Section 397/401 CrPC has been filed against the judgment and order dated 08.01.2008 passed by the Additional Sessions Judge, Court No. 5, Barabanki in Criminal Appeal No.78 of 1999 filed by the revisionist against the judgment and order dated 08.12.1999 passed by the 1st Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Barabanki whereby the revisionist was convicted for the offence under Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, and he was sentenced to undergo six months rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs.1,000/-, and in the event of non-payment of fine three months further imprisonment.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge, Court No. 5, Barabanki
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. While maintaining the conviction, the appellate Court has modified the sentence from the six months rigorous imprisonment to six months simple imprisonment.
3. Learned counsel for the revisionist submits that the revisionist is 50% disabled person.
The incident is of the year 1995.
This revision has been pending since the year 2008, the sentence may be reduced to the sentence already undergone while maintaining the conviction.
The learned counsel further submits that the revisionist has already undergone three months imprisonment.

4. On the other hand, Mr. Ashwani Kumar Singh, learned Additional Government Advocate,
submits that the revisionist has been found guilty of adulterating food items by the Courts below,
and this Court should not exercise revisional power to interfere with the judgment and orders passed by the Courts below.
5. I have considered the submissions of learned counsel for the parties, and perused the record.
6. From the supplementary affidavit in which medical certificate of the revisionist has been annexed as Annexure SA-1, it is evident that the revisionist is having 50% disability.
The incident is of the year 1995.
The revisionist has already undergone three months imprisonment, out of six months imprisonment.

7. Considering the age of the case, and disability of the revisionist, while maintaining the conviction,
the sentence is modified to the sentence already undergone, however, the fine is increased from Rs.1,000/- to Rs.5,000/- which shall be deposited by the revisionist with the trial Court, within four weeks from today.
8. With the aforesaid modification and observation, this revision stands disposed of.
[Dinesh Kumar Singh, J.]
